newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Lott sees chance for budget soon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Lott sees chance for budget soon.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Tuesday he sees an opportunity to conclude a budget agreement with the White House and Democrats within 24 hours.

Speaking to reporters after the weekly Republican policy lunch, the Mississippi Republican, said he expected to talk with President Clinton before the end of the day. Senate Budget Committee chairman Pete Domenici, Republican of New Mexico, said discussions on proposed tax cuts were "within a range" of dollars where an agreement could be reached.
"We have an opportunity here in the next 24 hours to come to closure on this," Lott said as he warned that delays would make it more difficult to hold enough support to pass the budget.

He said his goal is to reach agreement with the White House and finish Senate action on the budget before the May 23 recess for the Memorial Day holiday. This is also the date by which the House and Senate aim to have passed a major fiscal 1997 supplemental spending bill which would provide about $8 billion for disaster relief and military operations.
Lott said the administration needed to reduce the spending it proposed for new programs and for existing domestic programs if there were to be an agreement.

He and Domenici reiterated Republican belief that any adjustment in the consumer price index should be based on recommendations for techical adjustments made by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. "There will be no legislated, mandated numbers for CPI," Domenici said.
